Home.heroLine: A quiet dining room in Zagreb’s Upper Town. Croatia, cooked slowly — and over fire.
Home.heroImageAlt: Hand-rolled fuži with shaved black truffle in a dark ceramic bowl, candles and wine glasses on a wooden table
Home.intro: We cook the country slowly — truffle from the Istrian hills, pašticada braised the Dalmatian way, the cheese and cream of Zagorje — and leave enough quiet around the table to taste it.

istra.body: In autumn the truffle hunters of the Mirna valley send us whatever the dogs found that week. We shave it at the table, over pasta rolled by hand that morning.
istra.alt: Ribbons of fresh pasta under slices of black truffle on a dark plate

dalmacija.body: Two days in wine and vinegar, six hours in the pot with prošek and dried plums. The recipe came from a grandmother in Split; the patience is ours.
dalmacija.alt: Beef braised with potatoes in a deep brown sauce, served in a dark dish

jadran.body: Line-caught off Vis and cut to order, dressed with little more than Istrian oil and a few capers picked from island walls.
jadran.alt: Tuna tartare with crisp shallots on a light chilli sauce

Home.signatureNote: On the menu since the first night. It will be on the menu on the last.
Home.definition2: The pause at the table after the first bite, when nobody needs to say anything.
Home.menuTitle: Short, seasonal, rewritten when the market changes.
Home.menuBody: Around twenty dishes, a six-course tasting menu and wines from small Croatian growers. Every allergen is listed.
Home.roomBody: A ground-floor room on Opatička Street, a few minutes’ walk from St Mark’s Square. Linen on the tables, one window onto the street, and no music loud enough to compete with conversation.

gallery.candles: Candles lit at half past six
gallery.dessert: Panna cotta with wild berries from Medvednica

Home.visitTitle: In the Upper Town, between the Stone Gate and St Mark’s.

Home.manifesto: We cook Croatia [[dough]] slowly — truffle from the Istrian hills [[truffle]], pašticada braised the Dalmatian way, bread and pizza from a wood fire [[fire]] — and leave enough *quiet* around the table to taste it.

dough.title: The dough rests
dough.body: Flour from Slavonian mills, water, salt and a little of yesterday’s starter. Two days in the cold before it ever sees the oven.
dough.alt: Hands cutting proofed dough balls in a tray

fire.title: Wood, never gas
fire.body: Beech and oak from Gorski kotar. The oven is lit at noon and still glowing when the last guest leaves.
fire.alt: A wood-fired oven glowing, pizzas baking inside

hands.title: Out of the fire
hands.body: Blistered at the edge, soft in the middle, finished at the pass with what the morning brought — burrata, pršut, a shaving of truffle.
hands.alt: A chef’s hands presenting a finished pizza on the counter

chefs.title: Seats, and no more
chefs.body: A small room means the kitchen cooks for each table, not for a queue. Nothing is plated ahead; nothing waits under a lamp.
chefs.alt: Two chefs working together at the counter of an open kitchen

Story.title: A restaurant named after the thing it values most.
Story.lede: Tišina began with a simple idea: that Croatia is several cuisines, not one, and that each deserves to be cooked with the patience of the place it comes from.
Story.chapter1Body: Istria gives us truffles, olive oil and Malvazija. Dalmatia, slow braises and the sea. Kvarner, scampi sweet enough to eat raw. Zagorje and Slavonia, cream, cheese, flour and pork. The menu moves between them with the seasons, and the tasting menu walks through five of them in one evening.
Story.chapter2Body: We buy from fishermen on Vis and Ugljan, cheesemakers on Pag, a truffle family in the Mirna valley and vegetable growers within an hour of Zagreb. When something is not good enough, it is not on the menu.
Story.chapter3Body: Twenty-eight seats means nobody is rushed. Courses arrive when you are ready for them. There is no second sitting, and the table is yours for the evening.
Story.quote: Good cooking needs time. So does good company. We try to give both.
Story.imageAlt1: A chef plating a dish by hand at a wooden counter
Story.imageAlt2: Red wine poured from a decanter beside grapes and pears

Visit.title: Opatička 14, in the Upper Town.
Visit.lede: A short climb from Jelačić Square, or two minutes from the top of the funicular.
Visit.gettingHere: The Upper Town is mostly pedestrian. On foot, walk up Radićeva and through the Stone Gate, or take the funicular from Tomićeva and follow the Strossmayer promenade. By car, the nearest public garage is Tuškanac, a ten-minute walk away. Taxis can stop at the corner of Opatička and Mletačka.

faq.a: Yes, when we have room. Four seats at the bar are kept for guests without a booking. On Friday and Saturday evenings we recommend reserving.

faq.q: Can you cook for allergies and dietary requirements?
faq.a: Yes. The menu lists all fourteen EU allergens for every dish and marks vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options. Mention any requirement when you book and the kitchen will plan for it.

faq.q: How do I book for more than eight people?
faq.a: Write to us through the contact page or call. The whole room can be reserved for up to twenty-eight guests.
The dining room and restroom are on the ground floor. There is one low step at the entrance, and we have a portable ramp — let us know and it will be ready.
We accept all major cards and cash in euros.

sections.title: What we collect
sections.body: When you request a table or write to us, we receive your name, email address, phone number (if given) and anything you write in the message. We do not use tracking cookies or third-party analytics on this website.

sections.title: Why we use it
sections.body: Only to answer your enquiry or confirm, change or cancel your reservation. The legal basis is taking steps at your request before entering into a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).

sections.title: How long we keep it
sections.body: Reservation requests are kept for twelve months, messages for twenty-four months, then deleted.

sections.title: Who processes it
sections.body: Our database (Supabase, hosted in the EU) and our email provider act as processors on our behalf. We never sell or share your details for marketing.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You may ask to see, correct or delete your data, or object to its use, by writing to {email}. You may also complain to the Croatian Personal Data Protection Agency (AZOP).
